Innovations in intradialytic hypotension management: pathophysiology, precision monitoring, and emerging therapeutic strategies.
desc: [Renal failure] Intradialytic hypotension (IDH) is one of the most frequent and consequential complications of maintenance hemodialysis, affecting up to 40% of treatments depending on the definition used. IDH is independently associated with myocardial stunning, cerebral hypoperfusion, loss of residual kidney function, vascular access failure, and increased mortality. Despite extensive investigation, heterogeneity in diagnostic criteria, incomplete mechanistic understanding, and reliance on intermittent blood pressure measurements continue to limit prevention and management. We performed a narrative review of clinical trials, observational studies, systematic reviews, and guideline statements addressing intradialytic hypotension in adult hemodialysis populations. Evidence was synthesized across pathophysiologic mechanisms, monitoring strategies, and therapeutic approaches, including conventional and digital health interventions. IDH arises from an interplay of ultrafiltration-plasma refill mismatch, impaired vascular responses, reduced cardiac reserve, osmotic and thermal shifts, and medication effects. Epidemiologic estimates vary due to inconsistent definitions, although a nadir systolic blood pressure below 90 mmHg shows the strongest and consistent association with mortality. Traditional intermittent cuff-based blood pressure monitoring underestimates the burden and severity of IDH. Advanced monitoring approaches, including continuous noninvasive blood pressure measurement, volume assessment tools, and integrated dialysis machine feedback systems, enable improved detection of subclinical and evolving hypotension. Recent machine learning and artificial intelligence models leveraging clinical and real-time intradialytic data demonstrate strong performance for IDH prediction and support individualized ultrafiltration and dry weight optimization. Overall, IDH remains a multifactorial and under-recognized driver of morbidity in hemodialysis patients, and integration of precision monitoring with AI-enabled analytics may improve hemodynamic stability and clinical outcomes.

Compared with the state-of-the-art multitask models, the hdADMET model achieved competitive performance with a significantly lower computational cost. Its practical utility was further demonstrated by accurately predicting the ADMET profiles of newly identified NPs mined from the literature studies. The promising candidate with high anticancer activity, low toxicity, and favorable metabolic properties was identified for further experimental validation. The hdADMET model offered an alternative way to prioritize leading compounds for clinical translation through HN embeddings and deep learning.

Trained on a broad set of experimentally reported MOFs and computational databases, MOFGen generated hundreds of thousands of MOF structures and synthesizable organic linkers. desc: [International emergency nursing] Polytrauma triage requires rapid prioritization under conditions of incomplete information, physiological instability, crowding, and high consequences of error. Machine learning (ML) is increasingly discussed as a means of strengthening emergency triage; however, the concept of ML-supported polytrauma triage decision support remains insufficiently defined for emergency nursing, particularly regarding its temporal and clinical boundaries within the emergency department. This concept analysis clarifies the meaning, defining attributes, antecedents, consequences, empirical referents, and boundaries of machine learning-supported polytrauma triage decision support. Walker and Avant's concept analysis method guided the analysis. A structured and traceable literature identification process was used to examine literature on polytrauma, initial emergency department triage, clinical decision support, machine learning in emergency and trauma care, digital nursing decision-making, and artificial intelligence safety. Sources were mapped using a concept-analysis matrix to identify concept uses, candidate attributes, antecedents, consequences, cases, empirical referents, and conceptual boundaries. Machine learning-supported polytrauma triage decision support was defined as a human-in-the-loop clinical decision support process operating within the initial emergency department triage window, in which ML integrates polytrauma-relevant information available at or immediately before the first triage decision and generates time-critical acuity or near-term deterioration estimates to inform immediate prioritization without replacing clinician judgment. Three core defining attributes were identified: polytrauma-relevant initial-triage data integration, time-critical triage risk or acuity estimation, and human-in-the-loop clinical decision support. Model validation, workflow fit and interpretability, and performance governance were distinguished from defining attributes and positioned as antecedent or implementation conditions and empirical referents for safe clinical use. The concept is distinct from conventional triage, trauma scoring, post-triage prognostic modeling, generic clinical decision support, and automated decision-making. Clarifying both its defining attributes and its temporal boundary positions ML as a support for the initial emergency nursing triage decision rather than as a substitute for professional judgment or a broader trauma management system.

BlindDDG: A Blind Evaluation-Based Method for Protein Mutation Stability Prediction.
source: PubMed · Journal of chemical information and modeling
desc: [Journal of chemical information and modeling] Protein thermodynamic stability changes upon mutation profoundly affect protein structure and biological function. Recent advances in deep learning and protein language models have provided powerful tools for computational analysis of mutation-induced stability changes. However, most existing methods focus on quantitative regression of free-energy changes, which places strong dependence on precise experimentally measured ΔΔG values, although reliably determining the direction of stability change is itself an important objective in many practical applications. Here, we propose BlindDDG, a novel framework that reformulates protein mutation stability prediction from quantitative ΔΔG estimation to direction-oriented stability change classification. First, we introduce a blind-evaluation strategy that models mutation-induced changes by learning the representation difference between wild-type and mutant proteins, rather than relying solely on their individual intrinsic properties. This formulation focuses on the direction of stability changes and reduces the dependence on precise quantitative ΔΔG measurements. Second, a Siamese architecture with shared parameters is employed to encode the wild-type and mutant states and capture subtle mutation-associated differences. Third, a local structure-aware cross-attention mechanism is developed to integrate mutation-centered structural information with global protein language model representations, enabling effective multimodal feature interaction. Experimental results on the independent S669 benchmark demonstrate that BlindDDG achieves strong classification performance, obtaining an F1 score of 0.5449, an MCC of 0.3929, an accuracy of 0.7721, and a recall of 0.5417 for stabilizing mutation identification. BlindDDG outperforms all evaluated methods in F1 score, MCC, accuracy, and recall, highlighting its effectiveness in capturing mutation-induced stability changes, particularly for imbalanced stability classification.

desc: [RSC advances] The traditional analytical methods for detecting environmentally or biologically important analytes are sensitive, but not suitable for rapid on-site analysis because they require complex instrumentation and laboratory facilities. Optical Schiff base-based chemosensors and biosensors are promising tools owing to their tunable photophysical properties, and colorimetry or fluorescence sensing modes. Recent literature on Schiff base-based optical chemosensors developed for the detection of environmental and biologically important analytes such as metal ions, toxic anions, environmental pollutants and clinically important biomolecules published from January 2020 to 31 July 2026 is critically reviewed. This review discusses structure-property relationships and sensing performance. In addition, important photophysical processes like intramolecular charge transfer (ICT), photoinduced electron transfer (PET), chelation-enhanced or chelation-quenched fluorescence (CHEF/CHEQ), excited-state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT), aggregation-induced emission (AIE), and analytical performance parameters, including sensitivity, selectivity, detection limits, linear ranges, response times, and applicability to real samples, were evaluated. Portability of novel sensing platforms, such as paper-based sensors, smartphone-assisted analysis, and nanomaterial-integrated sensors were specifically examined. Also, special attention was given to new approaches that combine molecular design with computational tools, chemometric data analysis, microfluidic devices and portable digital tools to enhance analytical performance and to increase applicability in real-world applications. Finally, the critical challenges and future perspectives of sustainable sensor design, novel sensing approaches using Internet of Things (IoT), Artificial Intelligence (AI), and Machine Learning (ML) for the future Schiff base-based optical sensors were surveyed.

Large Language Model-Driven Knowledge Graph Construction for Photoresist Materials.
source: PubMed · Journal of chemical information and modeling
desc: [Journal of chemical information and modeling] Vast knowledge dispersed across the unstructured literature remains an indispensable complement to photoresist development. However, the intricate relationships among formulation, processing, and performance are not only scattered throughout publications but also complicated by semantic heterogeneity and contextual ambiguity, hindering knowledge management that extends beyond simple retrieval. To address these issues, we employed large language models (LLMs) to construct a photoresist material knowledge graph (KG) covering synthesis, properties, and applications. From nearly 12,000 full-text documents, we extracted 320,000 entities, 178,000 relationships, and 1,172,000 attribute entries. By integrating this KG with an LLM via a dual-path retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) strategy, we achieved 95.33% accuracy on a domain-specific question-answering task, substantially outperforming the standalone LLM (76.67%). This work offers a reference framework for knowledge management and intelligent reasoning in the photoresist field.

title: Development of a fully AI-based three-dimensional workflow for personalized target set-ups in orthodontics: First results.
desc: [International orthodontics] To present a fully automated artificial intelligence (AI) workflow to generate personalized orthodontic target set-ups and compare the quality of the occlusal outcome with manual set-ups, using the American Board of Orthodontics Model Grading System (ABO MGS). The AI workflow takes an intraoral scan and performs tooth segmentation, landmark detection, tooth completion, and tooth alignment to generate a 3D-printable personalized set-up without human intervention. The occlusal outcome was evaluated on twenty non-extraction full jaw cases treated with customized fixed appliances by comparing the AI set-ups to manual set-ups made by experienced laboratory technicians. Both set-up series were scored with the ABO MGS for alignment and rotations, marginal ridges, buccolingual inclination, overjet, occlusal contacts, occlusal relationships, and interproximal contacts. The 'alignment and rotations' category was additionally analysed separately for the anterior (canine to canine) and posterior (premolars to second molars) segments. Paired comparisons used the two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test (α=0.05). Based on the total ABO MGS scores, the AI set-ups (mean: 14.95) and manual set-ups (mean: 12.20) showed high-quality occlusal outcomes, which were both far below the ABO passing score. AI set-ups showed significantly more penalty points for alignment and rotations (median: 8 vs. 5; P<0.001). This difference was confined to the posterior segments; anterior alignment was near-ideal for both methods. Other categories did not differ significantly (P=0.082-0.886). For the first time, a fully automated AI-based 3D workflow generated personalized orthodontic target set-ups for non-extraction cases with a clinically acceptable, high-quality occlusal outcome, in approximately four minutes. Posterior alignment remains the only shortcoming of the AI set-ups and is the obvious target for further algorithm refinement or brief manual correction.

title: Coordinated online manipulation in the era of generative AI: emerging challenges.
desc: [Frontiers in sociology] Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is rapidly transforming the communicative processes through which coordinated online manipulation is produced, personalized, and coordinated at unprecedented scale, raising growing concerns about its societal implications. This Mini Review critically examines empirical research published during the first 3 years of widespread public accessibility of GenAI to assess how these developments are reshaping Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior (CIB) across different societal domains. Three interconnected developments consistently emerge: the transformation of communicative production through scalable, personalized, and multimodal content generation; increasing AI-assisted coordination of influence campaigns; and new forms of communicative vulnerability associated with increasingly human-like synthetic communication. Together, these developments suggest that coordinated influence is becoming more adaptive, persistent, and difficult to recognize within evolving human-AI communicative configurations. Beyond synthesizing recent empirical evidence, the review identifies emerging conceptual and methodological challenges concerning communicative agency, coordination, and authenticity, while outlining future directions for sociological research. Overall, the growing use of GenAI in evolving CIB poses significant risks to public trust, opinion formation, and democratic discourse, underscoring the urgency of understanding and addressing this rapidly evolving phenomenon.

title: Thermodynamically Guided CRISPR Spacer Optimization: Strategy-Dependent Off-Target Trade-Offs.
source: PubMed · Journal of chemical information and modeling
desc: [Journal of chemical information and modeling] Most CRISPR-Cas9 design tools select guide RNAs (gRNAs) by ranking predefined candidates rather than actively optimizing them. Here we instead formulate SpCas9 spacer refinement as a constrained search problem, in which a limited number of nucleotide substitutions may be introduced outside the PAM-proximal seed region. The search is driven by a thermodynamically grounded objective that combines CRISPRspec-based specificity with penalties for suboptimal GC content and long homopolymer runs. Within this single setting we compare five search strategies: three reinforcement-learning (RL) policies, which are Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), Quantile-Regression Deep Q-Network (QR-DQN), and Rainbow Deep Q-Network (Rainbow DQN), together with a nonlearning score-guided search and a prompt-guided large language model (LLM). All five share the same objective, mutable positions, substitution budget, and evaluation protocol, so that only the search strategy differs. On 100 held-out IGF2R guides from a gene and chromosome excluded from training, every strategy significantly reduced the predicted off-target burden (38.6-78.3%) and improved independent specificity metrics without degrading on-target scores. The strategies nevertheless differed sharply in per-guide safety: the LLM achieved the largest aggregate reduction but introduced new off-target sites into 38% of guides that were initially free of them, whereas PPO, an on-policy RL algorithm, retained a strong gain with the lowest regression rate of 15%. These results show that the thermodynamic objective supplies a robust common optimization signal, while the choice of search strategy governs the trade-off between aggregate improvement and regression of already-favorable guides.

title: Medical Reasoning in Large Language Models: Development and Evaluation of the MedEvalArena Benchmark.
source: PubMed · Journal of medical Internet research

title: GPT-4-Assisted Versus Human Detection of Intraoperative Adverse Events From Spine Surgery Operative Reports.
desc: [Neurosurgery practice] Manual chart review remains the primary method of clinical data collection in spine surgery research but is time intensive and prone to human error. Large language models may enable automated extraction of clinically meaningful events from unstructured operative text. We evaluated the performance of generative pre-trained transformer 4 (GPT-4) in detecting intraoperative adverse events from spine surgery operative notes compared with trained human reviewers. A retrospective cohort of 1454 laminectomy cases performed at a single academic institution between 2016 and 2022 was analyzed. Deidentified operative notes were independently reviewed by 4 trained human reviewers and GPT-4 using standardized prompts to identify incidental durotomy and nondurotomy intraoperative adverse events. Discordant classifications were adjudicated by a senior reviewer to establish ground truth. Performance metrics including sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, and F1 score were calculated. Analyses were stratified by operative note length, and review time was estimated. Incidental durotomy occurred in 88 cases (6.1%). GPT-4 achieved 100.0% sensitivity compared with 89.8% for human reviewers, with lower positive predictive value (88.0% vs 100.0%) but similar specificity (99.1% vs 100.0%). For nondurotomy adverse events (n = 21), GPT-4 demonstrated higher sensitivity than humans (90.5% vs 57.1%) with equivalent specificity (100.0%). GPT-4 maintained stable performance across note length quartiles, whereas human reviewer sensitivity decreased for longer notes. Human reviewers required approximately 35 hours to review all notes, compared with approximately 2 hours for GPT-4. GPT-4 demonstrated higher observed sensitivity than trained human reviewers for detecting intraoperative adverse events from spine surgery operative reports while reducing review time by more than 90%. Large language model-assisted chart review may serve as a scalable human-in-the-loop adjunct to traditional chart review, improving the completeness and efficiency of neurosurgical outcomes research.

title: Automated Approaches to Extracting Arm-Level Numerical Results From Published Studies for Meta-Analysis.
desc: [Campbell systematic reviews] Systematic reviews depend on accurate extraction of outcome data from primary studies, yet this step remains largely manual and time-consuming. Automation tools exist for identifying and retrieving studies and for extracting non-numeric study characteristics, but few target the numerical arm-level results needed for meta-analysis. We developed and evaluated a hybrid approach for extracting arm-level results (number of events and number enrolled per arm) for binary outcomes from two-arm randomized controlled trials published as PDFs. Rule-based string processing in R locates and parses results tables and candidate sentences in the Results section; a large language model (ChatGPT, accessed through the OpenAI API) is then used only to structure the numerical information in the selected sentences. We evaluated the approach by replicating a Cochrane meta-analysis of favipiravir for COVID-19 (11 trials; all-cause mortality at 28 to 30 days). Table-based extraction was applied to five articles and in-line text extraction to six. The extracted data matched the published arm-level results for all studies except one, where the pipeline recovered a sample size (24) consistent with the trial's results table rather than its text (25). The replicated random-effects meta-analysis gave a summary risk ratio of 0.84 (95% CI 0.49-1.46), identical to the original review, with minor differences in study weights attributable to rounding. An independent test on infectious bovine keratoconjunctivitis vaccine trials showed partial transferability, with failures confined to scanned PDFs and complex table structures. The code and the list of extracted articles are publicly available on GitHub.
